title: Frontend expects finding.previousStatus AND finding.currentStatus to render a 'PASS -> FAIL' arrow transition view, but the backend only ever sends previousStatus + status (never currentStatus) - the condition is always false.
description: Every changed finding falls back to showing just a single current-status badge, losing the before/after context the comparison UI was specifically built to show.
affectedFiles: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/cloud-posture/scan-comparison.js:157-174 (compareRawScanFindings now sets both previousStatus AND currentStatus on every 'changed' entry)
fixEvidence: scan-comparison.js's compareRawScanFindings() (replacing the old inline shape() in scan.controller.js) now builds each 'changed' entry as `{ ...currentShape, previousStatus, currentStatus, comparisonStatus: 'changed', changeType }` (scan-comparison.js:168-174) — both previousStatus and currentStatus are set from normalizeStatus() on the baseline and current finding respectively. ScanComparisonModal.jsx:455-459 already checked `finding.previousStatus && (finding.currentStatus || finding.status)` — that condition is now true for changed findings, so the before/after arrow transition renders as designed.

category: Configuration inconsistency (flagged for infra verification, NOT a confirmed data-loss bug)
title: The backend and the Prowler scanning service's checked-in .env files point at two genuinely DIFFERENT MongoDB databases on the same cluster (vib_test_db_revamp vs vib_test_db) - confirmed by direct connection to both.

title: 5 of 6 cloud-posture pages have zero permission gating — the entire provider drill-down hierarchy, service-level views, security-checks list, scan detail (951 lines), and check detail (255 lines) pages render with no `PermissionGate`/`usePermission` anywhere; only the top-level `/cloud-posture` page is gated
description:
**Checklist row:** §1.2 — RBAC permission gates on every UI action, not just the top-level page-level read gate.
**Files:** `(private)/cloud-posture/page.jsx` correctly wraps its content in `<PermissionGate permission="scan.read" allowProjectGrant>`. Every other page in the module — `[provider]/page.jsx` (renders `CloudProviderDashboard` directly, no gate, confirmed absent in the component too), `[provider]/[service]/page.jsx`, `[provider]/[service]/security-checks/page.jsx`, `scans/[scanId]/page.jsx` (951 lines), and the `(detail)` route's `checks/[checkId]/page.jsx` (255 lines) — has zero `PermissionGate`/`usePermission` import of any kind, confirmed by direct inspection of each file (not just a grep miss on a wrapper).
**Root Cause:** Only the entry page received a gate when the module was built; the deep-linkable provider/service/scan/check detail pages were never given their own, relying entirely on the top-level page's gate even though Next.js route segments are independently navigable/bookmarkable and don't inherit a sibling route's client-side gate.
**Impact:** Not a data exposure — the backend enforces `scan.*` permissions extensively (48 `requirePermission('scan.*')` call sites confirmed across the cloud-posture backend module). But any authenticated user who navigates directly to a scan or check detail URL (bookmarked, shared, or guessed) with no `scan.read` at all sees the page attempt to load — including, on the scan/check detail pages, potentially sensitive cloud security finding details — before the underlying API calls fail, rather than an immediate access-denied matching the main page's behavior.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Wrap each of the 5 pages in `<PermissionGate permission="scan.read" allowProjectGrant>`, matching the main `page.jsx`'s existing pattern — either individually per page, or by adding a shared `layout.jsx` at `(private)/cloud-posture/` (this module currently has none) that applies the gate once for the whole route tree, plus one at `(detail)/cloud-posture/` for the check-detail route group.

title: No notification dispatch anywhere in the cloud-posture backend module — a scan completing, failing, or being auto-cancelled/stuck never notifies anyone; `notificationEmail` exists only as an unused config field
description:
**Checklist row:** §5.1 — Key lifecycle events dispatch a notification: assignment, due-date approaching/overdue, approval requested, approval decision, status change — each fires through the standard dispatch pipeline.
**Files:** A repo-wide grep for `notificationService`/`dispatch(` across `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/cloud-posture/` returns zero matches. The only 'notification'-adjacent artifact in the entire module is `cloud-posture-config.model.js:82`'s `notificationEmail: { type: String }` schema field — a config value with no code anywhere that ever reads or sends to it.
**Root Cause:** Scan lifecycle events (queued→running→completed/failed, and the scan-reconciler job's stuck/stale-scan cleanup) were never wired to the platform's notification dispatch pipeline; the `notificationEmail` field suggests email notification was planned but never implemented.
**Impact:** Given this module supports scheduled/recurring scans (`cloud.scan_schedules.active`, `cloud.custom_schedule.enabled` per this module's own entitlement gating) that can run unattended, a user has no way to learn a scheduled scan completed, failed, or got stuck/cancelled except by manually revisiting the dashboard — there is no push signal for what is explicitly a background, asynchronous, potentially long-running operation.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In the scan-completion/failure handler (wherever `scan.controller.js`/`prowler.service.js` finalizes a scan's terminal status) and in `scan-reconciler.job.js` (for stuck/stale-scan cleanup), add a `notificationService.dispatch({...})` call analogous to the pattern already used in `workflowTransition.service.js` for other modules — notifying the scan's initiating user (and optionally the `notificationEmail` recipient, if that field is meant to be honored) on completion, failure, or reconciler-forced cancellation.
